How Much Does It Cost to Paint an Apartment in Canada in 2026?

Updated 2026 CAD pricing to paint an apartment in Canada: cost per square foot, per room, labour vs. materials, and how Toronto and Vancouver compare to smaller markets.

Painting is one of the most common renovation jobs booked in Canada every year — and one of the easiest to get a wildly inaccurate quote for. Prices swing a lot depending on the city, the condition of the walls, and the finish you choose. Here's what painting an apartment actually costs across Canada in 2026.

Average painting costs in Canada in 2026

Most painters price by the square foot of wall area or by the room. As a rule of thumb:

  • Budget job (one coat, builder-grade paint, walls in good shape): $1.50–$2.50/sq ft
  • Standard job (two coats, mid-grade paint, minor patching): $2.50–$4.00/sq ft
  • Premium job (three coats, low-VOC or designer paint, full wall prep): $4.00–$6.50/sq ft

For a typical 850 sq ft one-bedroom apartment, that works out to roughly $1,800 to $4,500 including labour and materials, depending on finish and wall condition.

Cost by room

  • Bedroom (10x12 ft): $250–$550
  • Living room (14x16 ft): $450–$950
  • Kitchen (with cabinets excluded): $300–$650
  • Bathroom (moisture-resistant paint): $200–$450
  • Hallway/entry: $200–$400

What drives the price up or down

Wall condition

Nail holes, drywall patching, and skim-coating add time before a single coat goes on. A unit that needs significant prep can add $500–$1,500 to the total compared to walls that are already smooth and clean.

Ceiling height

Standard 8–9 ft ceilings are priced into most quotes. Anything above 10 ft usually requires scaffolding or extension equipment, which can add 15–25% to labour costs.

Paint quality

Builder-grade paint runs $30–$45/gallon (covering roughly 350–400 sq ft with one coat), while premium low-VOC or designer lines run $60–$110/gallon. On an average apartment, upgrading paint quality alone can add $200–$500 to the job.

City and region

Labour rates vary significantly across the country. Toronto and Vancouver typically run 20–35% above the national average due to higher labour and overhead costs. Calgary, Edmonton, and Ottawa sit closer to the middle. Quebec markets, including Montreal, tend to run somewhat lower than Ontario and BC for comparable work — often 10–15% below Toronto pricing for the same scope.

Labour vs. materials

On a typical painting quote, the split looks like this:

  • Labour: 65–75% of the total
  • Materials (paint, primer, tape, drop sheets, supplies): 25–35%

This is why buying your own paint and hiring someone only for the labour rarely saves much — materials are a relatively small share of the total bill.

How to get an accurate quote

To get a precise number from a painter, have this ready before the estimate:

  • Square footage of each room (or let the painter measure on-site)
  • Condition of the walls (patched holes, water stains, old wallpaper)
  • Whether ceilings and trim are included
  • Desired finish (flat, eggshell, satin) and colour changes (dark-to-light colour changes can require an extra coat)

With this information, a professional painter using AI-assisted quoting software can turn around a detailed, itemized PDF estimate on-site — often before they've even left the apartment.
